entries.reason: Native and matched-phone review: the visible forefoot remains planted, cropped high torso hides the global stance collapse; dust does not establish lost support.
entries.prompt: Edit the FIRST attached artwork as a structural action correction, retaining Neris, Riven, their equipment, Nightglass drawing treatment, city setting and dusk palette. The current giant looks supported despite dust. Make its loss of support unmistakable. Widen the camera enough to show the giant's shoulder, sloping spine, higher hindquarters and rear supporting legs together. Its shield-side foreleg must visibly FOLD at the elbow and wrist under the chest, not stand straight or merely lift one paw. Pitch the chest hard downward until it is just above the dry plaza, head plunging sideways lower than shoulders, hindquarters still high and rear feet scrambling behind. The other forefoot reaches wide in a failed catch. The whole body must read as one enormous quadruped collapsing forward, not a crouch or a fifth-legged creature. Keep tiny Neris low left braced behind the securely rear-held crescent shield; show the oblique pale deflection plane making actual side contact with the descending foot, tipping its support sideways. Riven is a separate tiny silver-haired teal silhouette driving toward the exposed shoulder seam with his one right-hand saber. Human size consistent with gate arches, about one fifteenth of giant shoulder height. Preserve the existing displaced big slab and a broad directional dust crescent, do not add a debris storm or brighter aura. Prioritize violent mass redistribution and a coherent complete load path. Keep the ground a quiet dry matte value plane. Return one corrected illustration, no labels.

The violet deflection plane must visibly originate at that grounded butt, travel obliquely upward and contact the manta wing; the wing bends upward at the contact while the body banks and far tip still breaks the aqueduct. Kellan center: restore his ONE broad straight sword, held securely with BOTH hands around the hilt, blade continuous to its point planted in the shallow cistern spill at the origin of the existing ice escape ramp. His torso bends with force into the blade, shoulders and legs loaded, not an empty-handed spell gesture. Show blade-water-ramp continuity clearly in the foreground without hiding the soldiers. Preserve their distinctive burgundy/ivory and sand/cobalt costumes, normal human proportions, existing foreground scale and dramatic threat. Do not silently remove the dangerous broken span, evacuation uncertainty or remaining creature detail. No extra effects to hide grip/contact. This is a structural repair, not a texture finish. One corrected artwork, no labels.
